inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL batch update maps several primary-key values through CASE expressions, assigns more than one column in one UPDATE, and preserves non-target rows with an ELSE branch.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a two-item catalog curation update. One UPDATE assigns shelf positions and publication labels by item ID, while an unrelated archived item proves the WHERE predicate does not widen; the source schema, identifiers, values, and tutorial data are not copied.

fixture_notes: Only catalog items 501 and 502 are targeted. Their two CASE assignments take different branches; item 503 remains unchanged because it is absent from the IN predicate.
determinism_notes: The target IDs are unique primary keys, every CASE expression has an explicit ELSE branch, and the final read orders by item ID; there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, item_title VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, shelf_position INT NOT NULL, publication_label VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, item_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO catalog_items VALUES (501, 'Silver Map', 6, 'draft', 'active'), (502, 'Blue Orchard', 5, 'draft', 'active'), (503, 'Retired Lane', 2, 'legacy', 'archived')

steps.sql: UPDATE catalog_items SET shelf_position = CASE item_id WHEN 501 THEN 2 WHEN 502 THEN 1 ELSE shelf_position END, publication_label = CASE item_id WHEN 501 THEN 'featured' WHEN 502 THEN 'standard' ELSE publication_label END WHERE item_id IN (501, 502)
SELECT item_id, item_title, shelf_position, publication_label, item_state FROM catalog_items ORDER BY item_id
